about.title: Personal Injury Help in Walnut Creek, California
about.longDescription: Walnut Creek sits astride I-680, and that freeway shapes daily life for its 68,910 residents. Commuters funnel onto Ygnacio Valley Road from the eastern neighborhoods, shoppers circle Broadway Plaza and N Main Street, and Treat Boulevard carries a steady stream of cross-town traffic. Public records for 2025, the most recent final year, show 310 injury collisions in the city, with 413 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Reports tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the work week empties onto the same few corridors at once. If one of those collisions was yours, or you were injured some other way — a fall at a store, a bike crash on a shared path, a dog that got loose — the days afterward can feel disorganized and lonely. LawProactive exists to make one step simpler. We are a free service, not a law firm. We listen to what happened and connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Contra Costa County. The attorneys we connect with work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You decide whether to move forward. There is no cost to ask.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Walnut Creek Claim

items.title: Two Years Is Shorter Than It Sounds
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. Gathering records and identifying everyone responsible takes time, so an early conversation protects your options.

items.title: Six Months If a Government Entity Is Involved
items.desc: If your injury involved a city vehicle, a public sidewalk, or a state road like I-680, a formal claim may be required within six months. Missing that window can end a case before it starts.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were 30 percent responsible, your recovery is reduced by 30 percent, but you can still pursue a claim for the rest.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering in Ordinary Cases
items.desc: For typical injury claims in California, there is no statutory limit on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life, and emotional distress. What that means for you is something an attorney can explain.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to happen in Walnut Creek?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the corridors with the highest counts are Ygnacio Valley Road, I-680, N Main Street, and Treat Boulevard. These are simply the streets that carry the most traffic and therefore log the most reports. Records also show crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We don't give legal advice or represent you; the attorney you're connected with does that. There is no charge for using our service.

items.question: How much does it cost to hire an attorney through this connection?
items.answer: The attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis. That means you pay no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. Your first conversation about your situation is free, and you are under no obligation to proceed.

items.question: I was hit on I-680 but I think I contributed to the crash. Can I still recover anything?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, yes. Your share of responsibility reduces the amount you can recover but does not eliminate it. An attorney can help you understand how fault might be assigned in your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to act after an injury in Contra Costa County?
items.answer: For most injury claims in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of the injury. If a government entity is involved — for example, a county vehicle or a hazard on public property — you may have as little as six months to file a claim. Because the deadlines vary, it's wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.
